entries.name: EnterWorktree
entries.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

name.description: Optional name for a new worktree. Each "/"-separated segment may contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, and dashes; max 64 chars total. A random name is generated if not provided. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

path.description: Path to an existing worktree to switch into instead of creating a new one. Must appear in `git worktree list` for the current repo — or, on first entry from the launch directory, for a repo nested inside it (multi-repo workspace). Mutually exclusive with `name`.

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_Linear__get_issue
entries.description: Retrieve detailed information about an issue by ID, including attachments, git branch name, and active Triage Intelligence suggestions when the issue is in triage. A nonempty fields selection overrides the include options; request optional fields directly in fields.

id.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues

fields.description: Fields to include in each result. Explicitly requested fields with no value return null. `id` is always included. Omit or pass an empty array for the default response.

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_comments
entries.description: List comments on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. Provide exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId`. `statusUpdateType` applies only to `statusUpdateId`; omit it for every other parent. For issues, projects, and initiatives this returns both top-level discussion threads and inline description comments. Inline (anchored) comments carry a non-null `quotedText` set to the snippet of description text they reference. Returned comments include `author` and nullable `onBehalfOf`; when set, `onBehalfOf` identifies the user the agent author acted for. Files uploaded in comment bodies are returned in `attachments` with titles and download URLs, not issue attachment IDs. Signed upload URLs expire after five minutes; call list_comments again to refresh them. Download documents using these URLs and process them with your own file tools.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return per page

cursor.description: Omit for the first page. To continue, pass the previous response's cursor when hasNextPage is true

orderBy.description: Timestamp to sort results by: creation time or last update time

issueId.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues (provide exactly one parent)

projectId.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

initiativeId.description: Initiative name, ID, identifier (e.g., I-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

documentId.description: Document ID or slug (provide exactly one parent)

milestoneId.description: Milestone UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve milestone names via `list_milestones` first.

statusUpdateId.description: Status update UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve status updates via `get_status_updates` first.

statusUpdateType.description: Set only together with `statusUpdateId`; omit for issue, project, initiative, document, and milestone comments. Type of status update named by `statusUpdateId`, as returned by `get_status_updates`. Omit to check both project and initiative status updates.

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_issue_statuses
entries.description: List available issue statuses in a Linear team

entries.name: mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_issue
entries.description: Create or update a Linear issue. If `id` is provided, updates the existing issue; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `team` is required, and `title` is required unless `template` is set. Note: use `assignee` (not `assigneeId`) to set the assignee — it accepts a user ID, name, email, or "me".

id.description: Only for updating an existing issue. Pass the issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Do NOT pass this parameter when creating a new issue.

title.description: Issue title (required when creating, unless template is set)

description.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string — use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe)

patch.description: Partial edits applied to the current content, in order and atomically (one failing operation aborts the whole save). Every anchor string must match the current content exactly once. Only valid on update, in place of the full content/description field

old_string.description: Exact text to replace. Must match the current content exactly once

new_string.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the match

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match

anchor.description: Exact text to insert before. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly before the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")

anchor.description: Exact text to insert after. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly after the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")
Text to insert at the very start of the content
Text to insert at the very end of the content

from.description: Exact text where the range starts (inclusive). Must match exactly once

to.description: Exact text where the range ends (exclusive, stays in place). Must match exactly once after `from`

new_string.description: Text replacing the range. Empty string deletes it

team.description: Team name or ID (required when creating)

template.description: Template name or ID. Applied on create only. The template fills in the content, fields, and sub-issues server-side. A `description` replaces the template body rather than merging with it, but an empty `description` keeps the template body. Labels merge with the template's own

cycle.description: Cycle name, number, or ID. Null to remove

project.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug. Null to remove

assignee.description: User ID, name, email, or "me". Null to remove

delegate.description: Agent name or ID. When the user asks to delegate to "Linear" or "the Linear agent", this refers to the "Linear" app user specifically. Null to remove

labels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]). Replaces the full label set; existing labels not included are removed. Omit to leave labels unchanged. Cannot be combined with addLabels/removeLabels; prefer those for incremental changes

addLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to add. Append-only; existing labels are never removed. Cannot be combined with a team change

removeLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue. Cannot be combined with a team change

dueDate.description: Due date (ISO format). On update, pass null to remove the due date

slaBreachesAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the SLA will breach. On update, pass null to remove the SLA

slaType.description: SLA day counting type: "all" or "onlyBusinessDays". Only use with slaBreachesAt; null means unset

parentId.description: Parent issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Null to remove

estimate.description: Issue estimate value. On create, pass null or omit for no estimate. On update, pass null to clear the estimate; omitting leaves it unchanged. 0 is a real estimate only on teams that allow zero estimates.

links.description: Link attachments to add [{url, title}]. Append-only; existing links are never removed

setReleases.description: Replace all releases on the issue with these. Cannot be combined with addReleases/removeReleases

addReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to add. Append-only; existing releases are never removed

removeReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue

blocks.description: Issue IDs/identifiers this blocks. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

blockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers blocking this. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

relatedTo.description: Related issue IDs/identifiers. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

duplicateOf.description: Duplicate of issue ID/identifier. Null to remove

removeBlockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers to remove as blockers of this issue

{"id":"SMA-824","uuid":"1a47c734-65f4-4cbe-bc90-368c4aaa72c4","title":"Bedrock translator sends an empty text block for an empty text part","description":"The Bedrock Converse translator sends `ContentBlock::Text` for every `ContentPart::Text`, also when the text is empty or contains only whitespace. Converse rejects blank text blocks, so the request probably fails. The item stays in the session, so each replay of that session fails again.

This is the Bedrock form of <issue id="55003e53-0a09-43fa-9be0-bef2317ecbf4" label="SMA-819" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-819/anthropic-translator-sends-an-empty-text-block-for-an-empty-user-text" />, which fixes the same problem in the Anthropic translator.

## Where

`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/translate/request.rs`, in the `UserMessage` and `AssistantMessage` arms of the translator.

## Required behavior

* The translator drops text blocks that are empty or contain only whitespace, in user and assistant messages.
* The translator does not send a message that has no blocks left.
* Apply the rule <issue id="55003e53-0a09-43fa-9be0-bef2317ecbf4" label="SMA-819" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-819/anthropic-translator-sends-an-empty-text-block-for-an-empty-user-text" /> uses for the edge cases: fail early when no message remains, and when a dropped final user message makes the request end with an assistant message.

## Also check

The <issue id="55003e53-0a09-43fa-9be0-bef2317ecbf4" label="SMA-819" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-819/anthropic-translator-sends-an-empty-text-block-for-an-empty-user-text" /> spec challenge found a `tool_use` / `tool_result` ordering bug in the Anthropic translator. The `AssistantMessage` arm flushed pending tool results before pending tool calls. The Bedrock `AssistantMessage` arm has the same order (`flush_user_results` before `flush_assistant`). Check whether Bedrock has the same bug, and fix it here if it does.

## Acceptance criteria

* A live check against Bedrock Converse confirms the error for a blank block and the fix.
* Unit tests cover empty text, whitespace-only text, a message with no remaining blocks, and the ordering cases.

{"id":"SMA-824","uuid":"1a47c734-65f4-4cbe-bc90-368c4aaa72c4","title":"Bedrock translator sends an empty text block for an empty text part","description":"The Bedrock Converse translator sends `ContentBlock::Text` for every `ContentPart::Text`, also when the text is empty or contains only whitespace. Converse rejects blank text blocks, so the request probably fails. The item stays in the session, so each replay of that session fails again.

This is the Bedrock form of <issue id="55003e53-0a09-43fa-9be0-bef2317ecbf4" label="SMA-819" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-819/anthropic-translator-sends-an-empty-text-block-for-an-empty-user-text" />, which fixes the same problem in the Anthropic translator.

## Where

`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/translate/request.rs`, in the `UserMessage` and `AssistantMessage` arms of the translator.

## Required behavior

* The translator drops text blocks that are empty or contain only whitespace, in user and assistant messages.
* The translator does not send a message that has no blocks left.
* Apply the rule <issue id="55003e53-0a09-43fa-9be0-bef2317ecbf4" label="SMA-819" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-819/anthropic-translator-sends-an-empty-text-block-for-an-empty-user-text" /> uses for the edge cases: fail early when no message remains, and when a dropped final user message makes the request end with an assistant message.

## Also check

The <issue id="55003e53-0a09-43fa-9be0-bef2317ecbf4" label="SMA-819" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-819/anthropic-translator-sends-an-empty-text-block-for-an-empty-user-text" /> spec challenge found a `tool_use` / `tool_result` ordering bug in the Anthropic translator. The `AssistantMessage` arm flushed pending tool results before pending tool calls. The Bedrock `AssistantMessage` arm has the same order (`flush_user_results` before `flush_assistant`). Check whether Bedrock has the same bug, and fix it here if it does.

## Acceptance criteria

* A live check against Bedrock Converse confirms the error for a blank block and the fix.
* Unit tests cover empty text, whitespace-only text, a message with no remaining blocks, and the ordering cases.

Source: the spec challenge for <issue id="55003e53-0a09-43fa-9be0-bef2317ecbf4" label="SMA-819" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-819/anthropic-translator-sends-an-empty-text-block-for-an-empty-user-text" /> (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-sma-819-anthropic-empty-text-block-design.md` on its feature branch).","priority":{"value":2,"name":"High"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-824/bedrock-translator-sends-an-empty-text-block-for-an-empty-text-part","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-824-bedrock-translator-sends-an-empty-text-block","createdAt":"2026-11-20T14:47:32.868Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-20T19:29:10.380Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":"2026-11-20T19:29:10.358Z","canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"In Progress","statusType":"started","labels":["area:providers","Bug"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","assignee":"Sven Maschek","assigneeId":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Helikon","projectId":"5d1fd72d-af2d-40f5-b562-fa04f8018610","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

content.content:
1	# SMA-819: drop empty text blocks in the Anthropic translator
2	
3	Status: revised after the spec challenge, 2026-11-20. Size: a small change.
4	
5	## Intent
6	
7	The Anthropic translator (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/translate/request.rs`)
8	sends `{"type": "text", "text": ""}` for an empty user text part. The Messages
9	API probably rejects empty text blocks with HTTP 400. The live check must
10	confirm this. The bad item stays in the session, so each replay of that
11	session fails again.
12	
13	These paths make a blank text part:
14	
15	- an empty user input;
16	- a turn-boundary checkpoint that returns `Inject([Text ""])` (PR #346);
17	- whitespace-only text that a model emits, which is then replayed;
18	- a session that another provider recorded.
19	
20	## Goals
21	
22	- The translator drops each `ContentPart::Text` whose `text.trim()` is empty.
23	  The definition of "blank" is Rust `str::trim()` (Unicode `White_Space`). The
24	  design accepts any difference from the API's own definition. This rule applies
25	  to user messages and assistant messages, new and replayed.
26	- The translator does not send a user message or an assistant message that has
27	  no blocks left. This is wider than blank text. It also removes messages that
28	  have only `Reasoning`, only `Audio`, or only unknown parts. Today those go out
29	  as `content: []`.
30	- The translator sends `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks in the order of the
31	  items. The message that removes an empty assistant carrier needs this fix (see
32	  "Ordering fix").
33	- The system text is treated as absent when `system_text.trim()` is empty. This
34	  is a one-line change at `request.rs:106`. It prevents a whitespace-only system
35	  block with `cache_control`.
36	- `build_body` returns `ModelError::Other` before any HTTP call when the
37	  translated `messages` array is empty. The error text is neutral, for example
38	  "no message with content to send (empty and whitespace-only text is not
39	  sent)". The text must also be correct for a request that has only
40	  `Item::System`.
41	
42	## Non-goals
43	
44	- No change to `tool_result` content. The live check records whether the API
45	  accepts an empty `tool_result` string, for information only.
46	- No change to the other providers. The Gemini translator has a related problem
47	  in SMA-820. The Bedrock translator
48	  (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/translate/request.rs`) also
49	  emits blank text. SMA-824 covers it.
50	- No change to `paigasus-helikon-core`. Items in the session stay as they are.
51	  The fix is on the wire only.
52	- No support for extended thinking across a tool loop. The translator drops
53	  `Reasoning` on input today, and this ticket does not change that.
54	
55	## Anti-goals
56	
57	- The translator must not put placeholder text in place of a dropped block. That
58	  would send words the user did not write.
59	- The translator must not block a final assistant message that a caller sends on
60	  purpose (a prefill).
61	- The fix must not make a request fail that works on `main` today.
62	
63	## Decisions (from the conversation)
64	
65	1. **Edge case (Sven chose option c, after the spec challenge).** `build_body`
66	   fails early with `ModelError::Other` in two cases:
67	   - the drops leave no messages;
68	   - the last conversation item (`UserMessage`, `AssistantMessage`, `ToolCall`
69	     or `ToolResult`) is a `UserMessage` that the translator dropped, and the
70	     request now ends with an assistant message. An `AssistantMessage` that the
71	     translator also drops after that user message does not count as a later
72	     item, so `user q, assistant a, user "", assistant ""` is rejected. A
73	     dropped assistant item with no dropped user message before it is a caller
74	     prefill and is sent.
75	
76	   A caller that ends the item list with an assistant message on purpose (a
77	   prefill) is not blocked. The translator reports the second case to
78	   `build_body`, for example with a flag on `TranslatedMessages`. Sven first
79	   chose option (b) and changed to (c), because a drop-induced prefill makes
80	   the model continue its old answer.
81	2. **Approach (Sven chose option 1).** Filter where the blocks are made. See
82	   "Approaches".
83	
84	## Approaches
85	
86	1. **Filter where the blocks are made (chosen).** `user_blocks` and
87	   `assistant_blocks` skip blank `Text` parts. The `UserMessage` and
88	   `AssistantMessage` arms do not push a message with no blocks. `build_body`
89	   checks for an empty `messages` array. The rule stays next to the code that
90	   made the problem.
91	2. **A cleanup pass on the finished JSON.** This catches blocks that other code
92	   adds later. But it reads untyped JSON and puts the rule away from the code
93	   that makes the blocks.
94	3. **Filter the `Item` list before translation.** This puts an Anthropic rule in
95	   a generic place and must rebuild `Item` values. It does not fit.
96	
97	## Ordering fix
98	
99	Today an `AssistantMessage` with zero blocks is still pushed as
100	`assistant: []`. A following `Item::ToolCall` folds into it. That hides an
101	ordering bug. When this change removes the empty carrier, the bug shows:
102	
103	```text
104	items: User q, Assistant[Reasoning], ToolCall tu_1, ToolResult tu_1, Assistant "done"
105	bad:   user[q], user[tool_result tu_1], assistant[tool_use tu_1], assistant[done]
106	good:  user[q], assistant[tool_use tu_1], user[tool_result tu_1], assistant[done]
107	```
108	
109	The same bug is on `main` today for a tool call that has no `AssistantMessage`
110	(`User q, ToolCall, ToolResult, Assistant "done"`). A second form is also on

# SMA-819: drop empty text blocks in the Anthropic translator

Status: revised after the spec challenge, 2026-11-20. Size: a small change.

## Intent

The Anthropic translator (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/translate/request.rs`)
sends `{"type": "text", "text": ""}` for an empty user text part. The Messages
API probably rejects empty text blocks with HTTP 400. The live check must
confirm this. The bad item stays in the session, so each replay of that
session fails again.

These paths make a blank text part:

- an empty user input;
- a turn-boundary checkpoint that returns `Inject([Text ""])` (PR #346);
- whitespace-only text that a model emits, which is then replayed;
- a session that another provider recorded.

## Goals

- The translator drops each `ContentPart::Text` whose `text.trim()` is empty.
  The definition of "blank" is Rust `str::trim()` (Unicode `White_Space`). The
  design accepts any difference from the API's own definition. This rule applies
  to user messages and assistant messages, new and replayed.
- The translator does not send a user message or an assistant message that has
  no blocks left. This is wider than blank text. It also removes messages that
  have only `Reasoning`, only `Audio`, or only unknown parts. Today those go out
  as `content: []`.
- The translator sends `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks in the order of the
  items. The message that removes an empty assistant carrier needs this fix (see
  "Ordering fix").
- The system text is treated as absent when `system_text.trim()` is empty. This
  is a one-line change at `request.rs:106`. It prevents a whitespace-only system
  block with `cache_control`.
- `build_body` returns `ModelError::Other` before any HTTP call when the
  translated `messages` array is empty. The error text is neutral, for example
  "no message with content to send (empty and whitespace-only text is not
  sent)". The text must also be correct for a request that has only
  `Item::System`.

## Non-goals

- No change to `tool_result` content. The live check records whether the API
  accepts an empty `tool_result` string, for information only.
- No change to the other providers. The Gemini translator has a related problem
  in SMA-820. The Bedrock translator
  (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/translate/request.rs`) also
  emits blank text. SMA-824 covers it.
- No change to `paigasus-helikon-core`. Items in the session stay as they are.
  The fix is on the wire only.
- No support for extended thinking across a tool loop. The translator drops
  `Reasoning` on input today, and this ticket does not change that.

## Anti-goals

- The translator must not put placeholder text in place of a dropped block. That
  would send words the user did not write.
- The translator must not block a final assistant message that a caller sends on
  purpose (a prefill).
- The fix must not make a request fail that works on `main` today.

## Decisions (from the conversation)

1. **Edge case (Sven chose option c, after the spec challenge).** `build_body`
   fails early with `ModelError::Other` in two cases:
   - the drops leave no messages;
   - the last conversation item (`UserMessage`, `AssistantMessage`, `ToolCall`
     or `ToolResult`) is a `UserMessage` that the translator dropped, and the
     request now ends with an assistant message. An `AssistantMessage` that the
     translator also drops after that user message does not count as a later
     item, so `user q, assistant a, user "", assistant ""` is rejected. A
     dropped assistant item with no dropped user message before it is a caller
     prefill and is sent.

   A caller that ends the item list with an assistant message on purpose (a
   prefill) is not blocked. The translator reports the second case to
   `build_body`, for example with a flag on `TranslatedMessages`. Sven first
   chose option (b) and changed to (c), because a drop-induced prefill makes
   the model continue its old answer.
2. **Approach (Sven chose option 1).** Filter where the blocks are made. See
   "Approaches".

## Approaches

1. **Filter where the blocks are made (chosen).** `user_blocks` and
   `assistant_blocks` skip blank `Text` parts. The `UserMessage` and
   `AssistantMessage` arms do not push a message with no blocks. `build_body`
   checks for an empty `messages` array. The rule stays next to the code that
   made the problem.
2. **A cleanup pass on the finished JSON.** This catches blocks that other code
   adds later. But it reads untyped JSON and puts the rule away from the code
   that makes the blocks.
3. **Filter the `Item` list before translation.** This puts an Anthropic rule in
   a generic place and must rebuild `Item` values. It does not fit.

## Ordering fix

Today an `AssistantMessage` with zero blocks is still pushed as
`assistant: []`. A following `Item::ToolCall` folds into it. That hides an
ordering bug. When this change removes the empty carrier, the bug shows:

```text
items: User q, Assistant[Reasoning], ToolCall tu_1, ToolResult tu_1, Assistant "done"
bad:   user[q], user[tool_result tu_1], assistant[tool_use tu_1], assistant[done]
good:  user[q], assistant[tool_use tu_1], user[tool_result tu_1], assistant[done]
```

The same bug is on `main` today for a tool call that has no `AssistantMessage`
(`User q, ToolCall, ToolResult, Assistant "done"`). A second form is also on
`main`: `ToolCall t2` after a pending `ToolResult r1` folds into the earlier
assistant message, before `r1`.

The fix has three parts. Together they make the wire order follow the item
order:

1. The `AssistantMessage` arm flushes pending `tool_use` blocks before pending
   `tool_result` blocks. The `System` arm and the end of the loop already use
   this order.
2. The `ToolCall` arm flushes pending `tool_result` blocks before the fold
   check.
3. The `ToolResult` arm flushes pending `tool_use` blocks first.

## Behavior details

- A `UserMessage` that has pending `tool_result` blocks keeps those blocks when
  all its text is blank. The message is sent with only the `tool_result` blocks.
  This covers the SMA-804 `Inject([Text ""])` path after a tool result.
- When the translator drops an `AssistantMessage`, a following `Item::ToolCall`
  folds into the last message if that message is an assistant message, and
  goes into `pending_tool_use` if it is not. The ordering fix keeps both cases
  correct.
- A dropped message can put two messages with the same role next to each other.
  The translator already sends two adjacent user messages for two adjacent
  `UserMessage` items. The design keeps that behavior and relies on the API to
  join the turns. The live check must confirm this.
- A text block that is not blank keeps its exact text, with its whitespace. The
  translator does not trim the text it sends.
- `cache::apply_cache_strategy` runs after the drops, so the `LastTurn` marker
  goes on a block that is really sent.

## Verification

### Live probes (before the code change)

The probes need a real key: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or Claude through Bedrock or
Vertex. A keyless proxy with `mock_response` does not reach Anthropic's
validation, so it cannot prove these claims. **If no real key is available,
stop and bring this back to Sven.** Record the request bodies and the
responses. Never record headers.

Use `claude-haiku-4-5` and `claude-sonnet-4-6` (the IDs in `tests/live.rs`),
with thinking off unless the probe says otherwise. The probe bodies are:

| # | `messages` | What it proves |
|---|------------|----------------|
| P1 | `[user [text ""]]` | the 400 for an empty block |
| P2 | `[user [text "  \n\t"]]` | the 400 for a whitespace-only block |
| P3 | `[user "a", user "b"]` | the API joins adjacent user turns |
| P4 | `[user "q", assistant "a1", assistant "a2", user "r"]` | the API joins adjacent assistant turns in the middle |
| P5 | `[user "q", assistant "Sure."]` | a final assistant message (a prefill) works |
| P6 | P5 with thinking on | a prefill with thinking |
| P7 | `[user "q", assistant "Sure.\n"]` | a prefill with trailing whitespace |
| P8 | `[assistant "a"]` | an assistant-first request |
| P9 | a `tool_result` with content `""` | information only (non-goal) |

**Stop conditions.** If P3 or P4 gets a 400, stop and bring it back to Sven
before you change the design. If P5, P6, P7 or P8 gets a 400, record it and
report it at the next gate. Decision (c) already blocks a drop-induced
prefill, so these results are for the record.

### Probe results (2026-11-20, real key)

| # | `claude-haiku-4-5` | `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
|---|--------------------|---------------------|
| P1 | 400 `messages: text content blocks must be non-empty` | 400, same text |
| P2 | 400 `messages: text content blocks must contain non-whitespace text` | 400, same text |
| P3 | 200 (turns joined) | 200 |
| P4 | 200 (turns joined) | 200 |
| P5 | 200 (prefill continued) | 400 `This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.` |
| P6 | not run | 400, same prefill text |
| P7 | 400 `messages: final assistant content cannot end with trailing whitespace` | 400, same text |
| P8 | 200 (treated as a prefill) | 400, same prefill text |
| P9 | 200 | not run |

No stop condition fired. P3 and P4 confirm the reliance on joined turns. P5,
P6 and P8 confirm decision (c): on newer models a drop-induced prefill is a
400, and on older models it continues the old answer.

### Live tests (after the fix)

Add `#[ignore]` tests to `tests/live.rs`. Record the output of a real run in
the PR. A skipped run does not count. The cases are:

- (a) user, assistant with `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`, blank user. This is the
  SMA-804 path.
- (b) case (a) with `CacheStrategy::LastTurn`.
- (c) user, reasoning-only assistant, `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`, assistant text,
  user. This is the ordering path.
- (d) user, assistant, blank user, real user. This is the replay path.

### Unit tests in `translate/request.rs`

Compare the full `messages` array with `assert_eq!`, not only lengths.

- `empty_text_part_is_emitted_as_empty_block` changes to assert that the block
  is dropped. Rename it to match.
- Whitespace-only text (`"  \n\t"`) is dropped.
- A user message with no blocks left is not sent.
- A user message with blank text and pending tool results keeps the
  `tool_result` blocks.
- Blank assistant text is dropped, and an assistant message with no blocks left
  is not sent.
- A reasoning-only assistant message is not sent.
- A replayed sequence (real user, assistant, blank user, real user) keeps only
  the real messages.
- Ordering: user, reasoning-only assistant, `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`, assistant
  text.
- Ordering: the same with whitespace assistant text.
- Ordering: a tool call with no `AssistantMessage`, then a `ToolResult`, then
  assistant text. This pins the bug that is on `main`.
- Ordering: a `ToolCall` after a pending `ToolResult` does not fold into the
  earlier assistant message.
- Fold target: a blank assistant after a kept assistant, then a `ToolCall`.
- A whitespace-only system text gives no `system` field.

### Tests for `build_body` and `invoke`

- `build_body` with only a blank user message returns `ModelError::Other`.
- `build_body` with only `Item::System` returns `ModelError::Other`.
- `build_body` with `Item::System` and a blank user message returns
  `ModelError::Other`.
- `build_body` with `[user "q", assistant "a", user ""]` returns
  `ModelError::Other` (decision c).
- `build_body` with `[user "q", assistant "a", user "", assistant "b"]` sends
  the request. The caller ended the list with an assistant message.
- `build_body` with `[user "q", assistant "a", ToolCall, ToolResult, user ""]`
  sends the request. The `tool_result` blocks make a user message.

  puts the marker on the previous real block, and no block has blank text.
- A wiremock test through `invoke` with `.expect(0)`: a blank-only request
  returns `Err` and sends no HTTP request.

   today, but the change needs them to avoid a regression, and they have the
   same cause.

4. The live probes use `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the repo-root `.env`. Load it
   into the process environment only. Never print it or write it to a file.

94	3. **Filter the `Item` list before translation.** This puts an Anthropic rule in
95	   a generic place and must rebuild `Item` values. It does not fit.
96	
97	## Ordering fix
98	
99	Today an `AssistantMessage` with zero blocks is still pushed as
100	`assistant: []`. A following `Item::ToolCall` folds into it. That hides an
101	ordering bug. When this change removes the empty carrier, the bug shows:
102	
103	```text
104	items: User q, Assistant[Reasoning], ToolCall tu_1, ToolResult tu_1, Assistant "done"
105	bad:   user[q], user[tool_result tu_1], assistant[tool_use tu_1], assistant[done]
106	good:  user[q], assistant[tool_use tu_1], user[tool_result tu_1], assistant[done]
107	```
108	
109	The same bug is on `main` today for a tool call that has no `AssistantMessage`
110	(`User q, ToolCall, ToolResult, Assistant "done"`). A second form is also on
111	`main`: `ToolCall t2` after a pending `ToolResult r1` folds into the earlier
112	assistant message, before `r1`.
113	
114	The fix has three parts. Together they make the wire order follow the item
115	order:
116	
117	1. The `AssistantMessage` arm flushes pending `tool_use` blocks before pending
118	   `tool_result` blocks. The `System` arm and the end of the loop already use
119	   this order.
120	2. The `ToolCall` arm flushes pending `tool_result` blocks before the fold
121	   check.
122	3. The `ToolResult` arm flushes pending `tool_use` blocks first.
123	
124	## Behavior details
125	
126	- A `UserMessage` that has pending `tool_result` blocks keeps those blocks when
127	  all its text is blank. The message is sent with only the `tool_result` blocks.
128	  This covers the SMA-804 `Inject([Text ""])` path after a tool result.
129	- When the translator drops an `AssistantMessage`, a following `Item::ToolCall`
130	  folds into the last message if that message is an assistant message, and
131	  goes into `pending_tool_use` if it is not. The ordering fix keeps both cases
132	  correct.
133	- A dropped message can put two messages with the same role next to each other.
134	  The translator already sends two adjacent user messages for two adjacent
135	  `UserMessage` items. The design keeps that behavior and relies on the API to
136	  join the turns. The live check must confirm this.
137	- A text block that is not blank keeps its exact text, with its whitespace. The
138	  translator does not trim the text it sends.
139	- `cache::apply_cache_strategy` runs after the drops, so the `LastTurn` marker
140	  goes on a block that is really sent.
141	
142	## Verification
143	
144	### Live probes (before the code change)
145	
146	The probes need a real key: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or Claude through Bedrock or
147	Vertex. A keyless proxy with `mock_response` does not reach Anthropic's
148	validation, so it cannot prove these claims. **If no real key is available,
149	stop and bring this back to Sven.** Record the request bodies and the
150	responses. Never record headers.
151	
152	Use `claude-haiku-4-5` and `claude-sonnet-4-6` (the IDs in `tests/live.rs`),
153	with thinking off unless the probe says otherwise. The probe bodies are:
154	
155	| # | `messages` | What it proves |
156	|---|------------|----------------|
157	| P1 | `[user [text ""]]` | the 400 for an empty block |
158	| P2 | `[user [text "  \n\t"]]` | the 400 for a whitespace-only block |
159	| P3 | `[user "a", user "b"]` | the API joins adjacent user turns |
160	| P4 | `[user "q", assistant "a1", assistant "a2", user "r"]` | the API joins adjacent assistant turns in the middle |
161	| P5 | `[user "q", assistant "Sure."]` | a final assistant message (a prefill) works |
162	| P6 | P5 with thinking on | a prefill with thinking |
163	| P7 | `[user "q", assistant "Sure.\n"]` | a prefill with trailing whitespace |
164	| P8 | `[assistant "a"]` | an assistant-first request |
165	| P9 | a `tool_result` with content `""` | information only (non-goal) |
166	
167	**Stop conditions.** If P3 or P4 gets a 400, stop and bring it back to Sven
168	before you change the design. If P5, P6, P7 or P8 gets a 400, record it and
169	report it at the next gate. Decision (c) already blocks a drop-induced
170	prefill, so these results are for the record.
171	
172	### Probe results (2026-11-20, real key)
173	
174	| # | `claude-haiku-4-5` | `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
175	|---|--------------------|---------------------|
176	| P1 | 400 `messages: text content blocks must be non-empty` | 400, same text |
177	| P2 | 400 `messages: text content blocks must contain non-whitespace text` | 400, same text |
178	| P3 | 200 (turns joined) | 200 |
179	| P4 | 200 (turns joined) | 200 |
180	| P5 | 200 (prefill continued) | 400 `This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.` |
181	| P6 | not run | 400, same prefill text |
182	| P7 | 400 `messages: final assistant content cannot end with trailing whitespace` | 400, same text |
183	| P8 | 200 (treated as a prefill) | 400, same prefill text |
184	| P9 | 200 | not run |
185	
186	No stop condition fired. P3 and P4 confirm the reliance on joined turns. P5,
187	P6 and P8 confirm decision (c): on newer models a drop-induced prefill is a
188	400, and on older models it continues the old answer.
189	
190	### Live tests (after the fix)
191	
192	Add `#[ignore]` tests to `tests/live.rs`. Record the output of a real run in
193	the PR. A skipped run does not count. The cases are:
194	
195	- (a) user, assistant with `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`, blank user. This is the
196	  SMA-804 path.
197	- (b) case (a) with `CacheStrategy::LastTurn`.
198	- (c) user, reasoning-only assistant, `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`, assistant text,
199	  user. This is the ordering path.
200	- (d) user, assistant, blank user, real user. This is the replay path.
201	
202	### Unit tests in `translate/request.rs`
203	
204	Compare the full `messages` array with `assert_eq!`, not only lengths.
205	
206	- `empty_text_part_is_emitted_as_empty_block` changes to assert that the block
207	  is dropped. Rename it to match.
208	- Whitespace-only text (`"  \n\t"`) is dropped.
209	- A user message with no blocks left is not sent.
210	- A user message with blank text and pending tool results keeps the
211	  `tool_result` blocks.
212	- Blank assistant text is dropped, and an assistant message with no blocks left
213	  is not sent.
214	- A reasoning-only assistant message is not sent.
215	- A replayed sequence (real user, assistant, blank user, real user) keeps only
216	  the real messages.
217	- Ordering: user, reasoning-only assistant, `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`, assistant
218	  text.
219	- Ordering: the same with whitespace assistant text.
220	- Ordering: a tool call with no `AssistantMessage`, then a `ToolResult`, then
221	  assistant text. This pins the bug that is on `main`.
222	- Ordering: a `ToolCall` after a pending `ToolResult` does not fold into the
223	  earlier assistant message.
224	- Fold target: a blank assistant after a kept assistant, then a `ToolCall`.
225	- A whitespace-only system text gives no `system` field.
226	
227	### Tests for `build_body` and `invoke`
228	
229	- `build_body` with only a blank user message returns `ModelError::Other`.
230	- `build_body` with only `Item::System` returns `ModelError::Other`.
231	- `build_body` with `Item::System` and a blank user message returns
232	  `ModelError::Other`.
233	- `build_body` with `[user "q", assistant "a", user ""]` returns
234	  `ModelError::Other` (decision c).
235	- `build_body` with `[user "q", assistant "a", user "", assistant "b"]` sends
236	  the request. The caller ended the list with an assistant message.
237	- `build_body` with `[user "q", assistant "a", ToolCall, ToolResult, user ""]`
238	  sends the request. The `tool_result` blocks make a user message.
239	- `build_body` with `CacheStrategy::LastTurn` and a trailing blank user message
240	  puts the marker on the previous real block, and no block has blank text.
241	- A wiremock test through `invoke` with `.expect(0)`: a blank-only request
242	  returns `Err` and sends no HTTP request.
243	
244	## Settled at Gate 1
245	
246	1. Decision 1 is option (c). See "Decisions".
247	2. All three parts of the ordering fix are in SMA-819. Two parts are on `main`
248	   today, but the change needs them to avoid a regression, and they have the
249	   same cause.
250	3. The Bedrock translator gets a separate Linear issue.
251	4. The live probes use `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the repo-root `.env`. Load it
252	   into the process environment only. Never print it or write it to a file.
253	
254	## Left to the builder
255	
256	- The exact error text, within the meaning given above.
257	- The name of the helper that checks for blank text.
258	- Whether the translator emits a `tracing::debug!` line when it drops a block.
259	  If it does, the line contains counts only, never text.
260	
261	## Documentation
262	
263	- The crate `README.md` and the mdBook do not describe this translation rule.
264	  Check both. If nothing describes it, no edit is necessary.
265	- The fix is a `fix(providers)` change, so release-plz bumps the Anthropic crate
266	  and the facade as usual. No hand version bump.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/smaschek/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/7.0.2/skills/brainstorming

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

Before you start implementing, you must, in order:

1. Lay out the approaches in a message of their own, and have your
   human partner pick one (see Lay out the approaches).
2. Write the design doc, short or full (see Size the Work).
3. Get their approval of that doc.
4. Invoke the superpowers:writing-plans skill.

If nothing is open when you write your first message and there's one
sensible way, steps 1 to 3 happen in that message (see Your First
Message).

Two things aren't implementing: a spike they said yes to (see Spike to
feel things out), and doing what they asked once they've opted out of
the questions.

## Look Before You Ask

In an existing project, or when they've given you context (a spec, a plan,
a handoff, files they pointed at, earlier conversation), dig in before your
first message. Read what they referred to and the code or material it
connects to, and keep reading until you can explain how the relevant
parts work today and what this change would touch. Never ask what the
project or their context already answers, or reopen what they've
already decided.

## Your First Message

Move the work forward, with one of these:

- **They've already said what they want** (a spec, a plan, a detailed
  request): aim for about 200 words for the whole message. Echo their
  request back in your own words, so they can see whether you've got its
  shape: what they want, who it's for, and why, as far as they've said.
  Add what you found that bears on it: how the relevant parts work today
  and what the change would touch. If you found something they may not
  have considered that would change what they're asking for or how it
  has to be built, like a constraint, a conflict, or a cheaper path, say
  so plainly. How to build it comes later, once you understand what they
  want (see Lay out the approaches). End with one line inviting
  corrections. Then, if they haven't told you why they want it, even if
  you can guess, ask about that: one open question in their own terms,
  with nothing to pick from. If they have told you, and their request
  and the project leave open something whose answer would change what
  gets built, ask about the one that would change it most; when its
  choices can be named, sketch each concretely, with what it trades off
  and which you'd pick. If nothing like that is open, there's one
  sensible way: end with the short design itself (the approach, a line on
  why the others don't fit, and the design in a few lines) and ask them
  to approve it. Their approval covers the approach and the design: write
  the short design doc as approved and go on to the plan.
  Specs are often incomplete, so confirm before you build on one.
- **They haven't:** one open question, in their own terms, about the
  biggest thing their request leaves unsettled. Say why you're asking:
  what the answer would change about what you build. For "a website for
  my bakery": "If it's mostly for people deciding whether to stop by,
  I'd lead with hours and what's in the case today; taking orders is a
  different site. What do you want someone to do when they land on it?"

How the message ends depends on whether their message asked for
brainstorming:

- **They asked for it** (by name, by invoking it, or by asking for a
  design discussion): end there. They want this conversation.
- **They didn't:** they may not want a conversation at all. End with a
  light, one-line offer to just get going instead, like
  "Or if you'd rather I just dive in, say so." If they take you up on
  it, this skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
  (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
  asked through the normal workflow.

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Ask a question only when the answer would change what gets built and
neither the request nor the project answers it. Otherwise, state your
call and your reason as a proposal they can correct, and move the work
forward. Process steps are always your calls: writing things up, where
files go, looking further, how to show something. Do them and say so.
Ask one at a time. Use plain language, pitched just a little above where
your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use process jargon.
You never need to quote this skill to your human partner.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Until you know why they want it, ask open
questions, with no example answers attached. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Once you know why, when a decision has
choices you can name, sketch each concretely, with what it trades off
and which you'd pick. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?",
propose something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Read from how they
talk which of those choices they want to make. Someone who raises the how
or asks about trade-offs wants the options with your pick. Someone who
talks about outcomes is handing you the how: make those calls and state
each in a line. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Make every question specific** to their project and what they've told
you. Ask Socratically, the way a sharp colleague would: build each
question on their last answer or on something you found, so it helps
them think through a consequence or a case they may have missed
("Voting closes before the meeting, and two members joined this month.
Does someone who joins mid-round get a vote?"). When the reason isn't
already plain, say what you're hoping to learn or what the answer would
change. A proposal they can correct, plus your reason for it, often
beats a question.

**Do recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking further
would help, go look: deeper into their codebase or project, their own
files and data, or the web. Say what you looked for and what you found.

**Lay out the approaches.** Once you understand what they want, and
before you write anything up, put the ways of building it in a message
of its own. Come up with several real alternatives and drop the weak
ones, including any that work against why they want it and any the
existing work rules out. Sketch the two or three that remain concretely
enough to picture, grounded in what the project actually does, with what
each trades off. Recommend one and say why, then ask which way they want
to go; if they've handed you the how, say you'll go with your pick
instead. When there's genuinely one sensible way, say so in that
message and explain why the others don't fit; the design comes in the
next one. This is for how it gets built; for what they want, get them
describing first.

**Show, don't tell.** Whenever seeing would help more than reading,
sketch it in text: a few lines of what they'd see. Offer the visual
companion (below) when the look itself is theirs to decide:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Only what they said goes in as theirs. Anything you filled in goes in
as your proposal, with your reason. End each chunk by asking what's wrong
or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, put a
text sketch next to the description. If the look itself is theirs to
decide and they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the
offer instead (its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next
message. Once they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want and they've picked an approach, say
how big the work is in plain words. They can override it.

| Size | The design doc |
|------|----------------|
| A small change | a short one: what you already covered together, written down |
| A project | the full written design (below) |

Short or full, the design doc has an **Approaches** part: the two or
three ways you considered building it, what each trades off, which one
they picked, and why. They pick in the conversation, before you write
the doc.

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

## The Written Design

Write a plain document a talented builder in the domain could plan

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

Before you start implementing, you must, in order:

1. Lay out the approaches in a message of their own, and have your
   human partner pick one (see Lay out the approaches).
2. Write the design doc, short or full (see Size the Work).
3. Get their approval of that doc.
4. Invoke the superpowers:writing-plans skill.

If nothing is open when you write your first message and there's one
sensible way, steps 1 to 3 happen in that message (see Your First
Message).

Two things aren't implementing: a spike they said yes to (see Spike to
feel things out), and doing what they asked once they've opted out of
the questions.

## Look Before You Ask

In an existing project, or when they've given you context (a spec, a plan,
a handoff, files they pointed at, earlier conversation), dig in before your
first message. Read what they referred to and the code or material it
connects to, and keep reading until you can explain how the relevant
parts work today and what this change would touch. Never ask what the
project or their context already answers, or reopen what they've
already decided.

## Your First Message

Move the work forward, with one of these:

- **They've already said what they want** (a spec, a plan, a detailed
  request): aim for about 200 words for the whole message. Echo their
  request back in your own words, so they can see whether you've got its
  shape: what they want, who it's for, and why, as far as they've said.
  Add what you found that bears on it: how the relevant parts work today
  and what the change would touch. If you found something they may not
  have considered that would change what they're asking for or how it
  has to be built, like a constraint, a conflict, or a cheaper path, say
  so plainly. How to build it comes later, once you understand what they
  want (see Lay out the approaches). End with one line inviting
  corrections. Then, if they haven't told you why they want it, even if
  you can guess, ask about that: one open question in their own terms,
  with nothing to pick from. If they have told you, and their request
  and the project leave open something whose answer would change what
  gets built, ask about the one that would change it most; when its
  choices can be named, sketch each concretely, with what it trades off
  and which you'd pick. If nothing like that is open, there's one
  sensible way: end with the short design itself (the approach, a line on
  why the others don't fit, and the design in a few lines) and ask them
  to approve it. Their approval covers the approach and the design: write
  the short design doc as approved and go on to the plan.
  Specs are often incomplete, so confirm before you build on one.
- **They haven't:** one open question, in their own terms, about the
  biggest thing their request leaves unsettled. Say why you're asking:
  what the answer would change about what you build. For "a website for
  my bakery": "If it's mostly for people deciding whether to stop by,
  I'd lead with hours and what's in the case today; taking orders is a
  different site. What do you want someone to do when they land on it?"

How the message ends depends on whether their message asked for
brainstorming:

  design discussion): end there. They want this conversation.

  it, this skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
  (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
  asked through the normal workflow.

That's the whole message.

Ask a question only when the answer would change what gets built and

call and your reason as a proposal they can correct, and move the work

files go, looking further, how to show something. Do them and say so.

your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use process jargon.

choices you can name, sketch each concretely, with what it trades off

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,

- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what

When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,

conversation.

content.text:
I have enough to describe the work. Here is my reading of SMA-824 and what I found in the code.

**What you want.** The Bedrock translator must stop sending blank text blocks. Converse probably rejects them, and a bad item in a session makes each replay fail again. The rules from SMA-819 apply: drop blank text, send no empty message, fail early when no message remains, and fail early when a dropped final user message makes the request end with an assistant message.

**What I found in `request.rs`:**

- The Bedrock translator already skips a message with no blocks. It also joins adjacent same-role turns. Thus a dropped message cannot make two user turns next to each other in most paths. This part is smaller than in SMA-819.
- **The tool order.** The `AssistantMessage` arm is correct. Both lists can be pending at the same time only when a `ToolCall` comes after a `ToolResult`. Then "results first" is the item order. But the `ToolCall` arm has the second bug form from SMA-819. A sequence such as `assistant[a, t1], result r1, call t2, result r2` becomes `assistant[a, t1, t2], user[r1, r2]`. I propose to port `round_is_answered`.
- **A third blank block that the issue does not name.** When the first message is an assistant message, the translator adds a placeholder user turn with `Text("")` (`request.rs:243-248`). A dropped first user message, for example `[user "", assistant "a", user "b"]`, reaches this path.
- A blank `Item::System` also goes out as an empty `SystemContentBlock::Text`. I propose to drop it, as in SMA-819.

Tell me if any of this is wrong.

**The question that changes the design most:** what must happen when the first sent message is an assistant message? If the live probe shows that Converse rejects the empty placeholder, that path never worked. Then I suggest that the translator fails early with a clear error. A placeholder with words would send text that the user did not write, and SMA-819 rejected that. The other choice is to keep the placeholder and leave the path out of scope. Which do you want?

I also need credentials for the live check. Which AWS profile, region and model ID do you want me to use?

#!/bin/bash
# Second round of live Converse probes for SMA-824.
export AWS_PROFILE=maip-dev-admin AWS_REGION=eu-central-1

probe() { # name, model, messages json, [extra aws args...]
  local name=$1 m=$2 msgs=$3
  shift 3
  echo "=== $name ($m)"
  echo "messages: $msgs"
  [ $# -gt 0 ] && echo "extra: $*"
  aws bedrock-runtime converse --model-id "$m" --messages "$msgs" "$@" \
    --inference-config '{"maxTokens":20}' \
    --query '{stop:stopReason,out:output.message.content[?text].text}' --output json 2>&1 \
    | tr -s '\n' ' ' | cut -c1-300
  echo
}

S=global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5
FIRST_ASSISTANT='[{"role":"assistant","content":[{"text":"Hello."}]},{"role":"user","content":[{"text":"Say hi."}]}]'
PLACEHOLDER='[{"role":"user","content":[{"text":""}]},{"role":"assistant","content":[{"text":"Hello."}]},{"role":"user","content":[{"text":"Say hi."}]}]'

probe B11 "$S" "$PLACEHOLDER"
probe B12 "$S" '[{"role":"user","content":[{"text":"Say hi."}]}]' --system '[{"text":" \n"}]'

content.text:
The probes are done. They settle most points, and they show one more bug on `main`.

**Probe results** (`global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5`, `eu-central-1`; plus Nova Lite and Pixtral Large for the first-message rule):

| # | Request | Result |
|---|---------|--------|
| B1 | user `""` | 400 `The text field in the ContentBlock … is blank` (all three families) |
| B2 | user `"  \n\t"` | 400 `text content blocks must contain non-whitespace text` |
| B7 | assistant `""` in the middle | 400 `text content blocks must be non-empty` |
| B12 | system `" \n"` | 400 `The system field can't be blank` |
| B3, B9 | two adjacent user or assistant turns | 200 (Converse joins the turns) |
| B5 | final assistant message (a prefill) | 400 `This model does not support assistant message prefill` |
| B8 | `tool_result` with `""` content | 200 (for information only) |
| B4 | assistant message first | Claude: 200. Nova and Pixtral: 400 `A conversation must start with a user message` |
| B11 | today's placeholder: user `""`, assistant, user | 400 (blank block) |

The Llama 3.2 profile is end-of-life, so I have no result for it.

**The new finding.** The placeholder user turn fails on every model. On `main`, each request that starts with an assistant message fails, for all families.

**How to build it.** There is one sensible way, which is the SMA-819 approach. The translator skips blank text where it makes the blocks, ports `round_is_answered` to the `ToolCall` arm, drops blank system blocks, and sets a flag for the drop-induced final assistant message. A cleanup pass after translation, or a filter on the `Item` list, does not fit, for the same reasons as in SMA-819.

**The open choice is the placeholder.** There are three options:

1. **Remove the placeholder, and send the assistant message first (my pick).** Claude models then work. Nova and Mistral return the clear server error above. No request that works today fails. The cost is that the error for Nova and Mistral comes from the server, not early.
2. **Fail early when the first message is an assistant message.** The behavior is the same for all families, and nothing goes over the network. But Claude requests that could work also fail, for example a replay whose first user input was blank.
3. **Fail early only for families that need a user message first** (by `ModelFamily`). This gives an early error and keeps Claude working. It adds more code, and the list of families can become out of date.

I recommend option 1, because it is the smallest change and the server error is already clear. Which option do you want?

# SMA-824: drop empty text blocks in the Bedrock translator

Status: draft, 2026-11-20. Size: a small change.

## Intent

The Bedrock Converse translator
(`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/translate/request.rs`) sends
`ContentBlock::Text` for each `ContentPart::Text`, also when the text is blank.
Converse rejects blank text blocks (probes B1, B2, B7 below). The bad item stays
in the session, so each replay of that session fails again.

This is the Bedrock form of SMA-819 (PR #353), which fixed the Anthropic
translator. The rules come from the SMA-819 design
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-sma-819-anthropic-empty-text-block-design.md`).

These paths make a blank text part: an empty user input, a turn-boundary
checkpoint that returns `Inject([Text ""])`, whitespace-only text that a model
emits and that is then replayed, and a session that another provider recorded.

## How the Bedrock translator differs from the Anthropic one

- The `UserMessage` and `AssistantMessage` arms already skip a message that has
  no blocks.
- The translator already joins adjacent same-role turns. Converse also accepts
  adjacent same-role turns (probes B3, B9).
- The translator adds a placeholder user turn `Text("")` when the first message
  is an assistant message. Converse rejects that block on every model (probe
  B11). Thus, on `main`, each request that starts with an assistant message
  fails.
- The `AssistantMessage` arm flushes pending tool results before pending tool
  calls. This order is correct here. Both lists are pending at the same time

| B8 | a `toolResult` with text `""` | 200 |
| B9 | `[user, assistant "Hi", assistant " there", user]` | 200 |
| B10 | two parallel tool calls, two results | 200 |
| B11 | `[user "", assistant "Hello.", user "Say hi."]` (today's placeholder) | 400, same text as B1 |
| B12 | system `" \n"` | 400 `The system field can't be blank.` |

The Llama 3.2 inference profile is end-of-life, so it gave no result.

### Live tests (after the fix)

Add `#[ignore]` tests to `tests/live.rs`. Run them with
`BEDROCK_MODEL_ID=global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5`, `AWS_PROFILE=maip-dev-admin`
and `AWS_REGION=eu-central-1`. Record the output of a real run in the PR. A
skipped run does not count. The cases are:

- (a) user, assistant with `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`, blank user (the SMA-804
  path);
- (b) user, assistant, blank user, real user (the replay path);
- (c) user, whitespace-only assistant, `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`, assistant text,
  user (the ordering path);
- (d) assistant first, then user (the removed placeholder; Claude only);
- (e) a whitespace-only `Item::System` and a real user.

### Unit tests in `translate/request.rs`

Compare the full `messages` array with `assert_eq!`, not only lengths.

- Empty text is dropped. Whitespace-only text (`"  \n\t"`) is dropped.
- A user message with no blocks left is not sent.
- A user message with blank text and pending tool results keeps the
  `ToolResult` blocks.
- Blank assistant text is dropped, and an assistant message with no blocks left
  is not sent.
- A replayed sequence (real user, assistant, blank user, real user) keeps only
  the real content.
- A blank or whitespace-only system text gives no system block.
- Assistant first: no placeholder. `assistant_first_gets_synthetic_user_prepended`
  and `tool_call_item_queues_onto_assistant_turn` change to match.
- Ordering: a `ToolCall` after a pending `ToolResult` does not fold into the
  earlier assistant message.
- Ordering: a multi-round tool loop with no assistant text alternates.
- Ordering: a `ToolCall` after a pending result, then the end of the input.
- Ordering: user, whitespace-only assistant, `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`,
  assistant text.
- Ordering: two parallel tool calls with their results stay in one round.
- Errors: only a blank user message; only `Item::System`; `Item::System` and a
  blank user message; `[user "q", assistant "a", user ""]` (option c).
- Not errors: `[user "q", assistant "a", user "", assistant "b"]`;
  `[user "q", assistant "a", ToolCall, ToolResult, user ""]`;
  `[user "q", assistant "a"]` (a caller prefill).

path and the normal path both return the error.

- The exact error text, within the meaning given above.
- The name of the helper that checks for blank text.
- Whether the error comes from `items_to_messages` directly or from a flag on
  `TranslatedMessages`. Both call sites in `translate/mod.rs` use `?`, so a
  direct `Err` is the simple choice.
- Whether the translator emits a `tracing::debug!` line when it drops a block.
  If it does, the line contains counts only, never text.
- On macOS, the Bedrock tests can fail for a reason that is not in the code
  (`NATIVE_ROOTS`, which depends on the checkout path). If they fail with that
  error, run them from a worktree under the scratchpad.

## Documentation

- The crate `README.md` and the mdBook do not describe these translation rules,
  so no edit is necessary.
- The change is a `fix(providers)` change (`providers-bedrock` is not in the
  scope allowlist). release-plz bumps the Bedrock crate and the facade. No hand
  version bump.

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES
The spec's claims about the current Bedrock code are correct. I checked each claim against `request.rs` by hand. No finding blocks implementation. The gaps are in four areas: what the probes prove for Nova and Mistral, the definition of "dropped", the live-test gating, and the precision of the unit-test list.

## Findings

### BLOCKER
None.

### MAJOR

- **The probes do not prove the anti-goal for Nova and Mistral** - B2 (whitespace-only text) ran only on Claude. B1 shows that the Bedrock service check rejects `""` at `messages.0` on all three families. B2 and B7, however, returned Anthropic model errors, not service errors. Thus whitespace-only text gets past the service check and goes to the model. Nova and Mistral may accept it. After the fix, `[user "  "]` and `[user "q", assistant "a", user "  "]` become early `ModelError::Other` on every family. | Why it matters: if Nova Lite or Pixtral Large accept whitespace-only user text today, the fix makes a working request fail. The spec says "No request that works today fails", but no probe supports this for those families. | Suggested fix: run B2 and a trailing `[user q, assistant a, user "  "]` on Nova Lite and Pixtral Large, and record the results. If they return 200, write this into the spec as an accepted consequence of option (c), or ask Sven for a decision.

- **"Dropped" has no definition, and Bedrock drops more part types than Anthropic** - The `UserMessage` arm keeps only `Text` and `ToolResult` (`request.rs:113-118`). `Image` and `Audio` are always skipped, and the crate does not advertise vision. The SMA-819 code sets the flag on `blocks.is_empty()`. If the builder ports that, `[user q, assistant a, user [Image]]` and `[user q, assistant a, user []]` become early errors. On `main` these go out as a prefill, and models that accept a prefill return 200. | Why it matters: these requests work on `main` and fail after the fix, which breaks the anti-goal. Also, the example error text "(empty and whitespace-only text is not sent)" names the wrong cause. "No message with content to send" is false for the trailing case, because messages remain. | Suggested fix: define "dropped" in the spec. Either it means "the UserMessage produced no block for any reason", or it means "all its parts were blank text". Write down the consequence for image-only messages. Require one error text for each case, and make both texts name unsupported parts. The two texts in `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/translate/mod.rs:37` and `:42` are a good model.

- **The live-test model ID is detected as `ModelFamily::Unknown`** - `strip_region_prefix` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/family.rs:88-95`) strips only `us.`, `eu.`, `apac.` and `ap.`. For `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5` the provider segment is `global`, so the family is `Unknown`. | Why it matters: live test (d) is "Claude only". The existing live tests gate on `ModelFamily` (`tests/live.rs:96-105`, `:173-183`). If (d) uses the same gate, it skips, and the spec says that "a skipped run does not count". The two existing family-gated live tests also skip with this ID. In production, `global.` profiles lose structured-output synthesis, forced tool choice and `parallel_tool_calls`. | Suggested fix: gate (d) on the model ID string or on an explicit env var, not on `ModelFamily`.   - an interleaved parallel round (`t1, t2, r1, t3, r2, r3`) stays one round (SMA-819 `interleaved_parallel_round_is_not_split`);
  - a dropped assistant inside an open round does not split the round;

  | Why it matters: the ordering fix changes the wire for requests that return 200 today. Without these tests, a wrong port passes CI. | Suggested fix: port the SMA-819 tests in `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/translate/request.rs` by name, with Bedrock expected arrays. Then add the Bedrock-only cases above. The `items_to_messages` doc (`request.rs:35-38`) and the `build_request` `# Errors` list (`translate/mod.rs:85-89`) do not list the new error cases. | Suggested fix: list these sites in the spec.

A new `tracing::debug!` must use `target: "paigasus::bedrock::translate"`. If it does not, `tests/workspace-lints/tests/tracing_target_coverage.rs` fails. `invoke` calls `build_request` before it makes the stream (`model.rs:49`). It also implies that the live tests run with an admin role. | Suggested fix: write "an AWS profile that can call `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` on the model". Keep the profile name out of the committed spec.

One shape is a blank first user message followed by an assistant reply, for example `[user "", assistant "Hi", user "x"]` from a session that another provider recorded. That source is one that the spec lists. Today this fails with the B1 error. After the fix it fails with "A conversation must start with a user message". # Third round of live Converse probes for SMA-824 (spec-challenge follow-up).
export AWS_PROFILE=maip-dev-admin AWS_REGION=eu-central-1

probe() { # name, model, messages json, [extra aws args...]
  local name=$1 m=$2 msgs=$3
  shift 3
  echo "=== $name ($m)"
  echo "messages: $msgs"
  aws bedrock-runtime converse --model-id "$m" --messages "$msgs" "$@" \
    --inference-config '{"maxTokens":20}' \
    --query '{stop:stopReason,out:output.message.content[?text].text}' --output json 2>&1 \
